lanes.summary: The diff successfully implements the work sync engine in a pure, testable manner, but contains a logic hole in the bijection (a `no-roadmap` issue bypasses checks), a specification contradiction regarding authoritative fields, and tests that do not actually verify their namesake logic. Truncation of issues via `gh` reads as false coherence for `OrphanGithub`.

findings.claim: An open item pointing to a `no-roadmap` open issue escapes `OrphanRoadmap`, `OrphanGithub`, and `Collision`. It lands in `matched_pairs` because `snapshot.issue(n)` ignores `in_universe()`.
The spec contradicts itself: §5.3 lists `release` as roadmap-authoritative, but §4.1 correctly calls it a projection. The code implements §4.1.

The snapshot truncates issues at 5000, which hides `OrphanGithub` findings and reads as false coherence. Milestone truncation (100) does nothing because `snapshot.milestones` is completely ignored by the engine.
The test `full_is_the_union_of_both_directions` never computes the union. It only calls `Direction::Full` and asserts the result, surviving a mutant where `YamlToGithub` is broken.

The commit message for 6d6d75168 falsely claims to rewrite three `notes:` fields; it actually rewrites one `notes:` field and three `acceptance_criteria` items. The arm 4 control script will fail on legitimate future manual edits that serde reformats.

lanes.summary: Adversarial review completed. The diff fails the specification due to several critical flaws: an item can escape all finding classes by naming a 'no-roadmap' issue, 'gh issue list' truncation masks 'ORPHAN-GITHUB' findings as coherence, and the control script's Arm 4 passes for the wrong reason by blinding the engine to real issues.

findings.claim: The bijection check allows an open item to escape all finding classes if it names an open issue labelled 'no-roadmap'
findings.fix: Check !issue.in_universe() for the item loop, or verify issue validity against g_issues.

findings.claim: gh issue list silently truncates at 5000, hiding ORPHAN-GITHUB issues and reading as coherence
findings.fix: Add pagination to the gh issue list command to fetch all issues.

findings.claim: Control script Arm 4 passes for the wrong reason because the snapshot is missing all real issues, forcing IssueAbsent skips
findings.fix: Provide a realistic mock snapshot in Arm 4 or change the verification strategy.

lanes.summary: Completed an adversarial review of the PMAT-720 PR against the specification. Found multiple flaws leading to a FAIL verdict: the grace window is incorrectly applied per-pair instead of per-field, breaking staleness calculations; Arm 4 of the control script passes vacuously due to an empty snapshot bypassing all drift mutation; test coverage is missing for JSON stdout and release skipping; and the open-item universe widening breaks downstream consistency with CB-2114. All 9 questions have been answered with concrete file/line evidence.

findings.claim: The open-item universe widening in check() defies the spec's strict {planned, inprogress} scope for CB-2114, causing inconsistent downstream inheritance.
The grace window is applied per-pair. A recent update to one field resets the age clock, hiding stale drift on the other field.
The spec §5.3 contradicts §4.1 by listing release as roadmap-authoritative. The code implements §4.1, but §5.3 needs amendment.
The test check_only_passes_on_a_bijection sets json = true but fails to capture or assert stdout, surviving a mutant that breaks JSON formatting.
No test in tests.rs asserts the Skip reason for DriftField::Release in the YamlToGithub direction.

Arm 4 of the control script passes for the wrong reason: by feeding a 1-issue fake snapshot, all real items become IssueAbsent (which plan() Skips on github-to-yaml), bypassing all drift mutations to fake a perfect round-trip.
Arm 4 will fail on a legitimate future edit if the user hand-wraps a YAML string, as the serializer will reformat it to a single line and break the byte-for-byte diff.

uncovered.item: Q1 set predicate, widened open-item universe

orchestrator_adjudication.finding: An open item naming an open issue labelled no-roadmap lands in matched_pairs; it escapes all three set classes (mod.rs Some(n) arm)
orchestrator_adjudication.action: OrphanReason::IssueExcluded: the item is ORPHAN-ROADMAP; every direction skips it naming the label and #n; test an_open_item_naming_a_no_roadmap_issue_is_an_orphan_roadmap (check + plan), mutant 'treat excluded as matched' dies under it

orchestrator_adjudication.finding: gh issue list --limit 5000 and milestones per_page=100 truncate silently; a truncated snapshot reads as coherence
orchestrator_adjudication.action: refuse_truncation(count, cap, what): a result at the cap is an error naming the cap, never a report; test a_snapshot_at_the_page_cap_is_refused; the engine's milestones field stays unused until CB-2114 (step 5) needs RR-RELEASE validity

orchestrator_adjudication.finding: Control arm 4 passes for the wrong reason: its 1-issue snapshot makes every real item IssueAbsent, so no fixer path is exercised on the real roadmap
orchestrator_adjudication.action: arm 4 proves the serializer (byte-for-byte round trip of 5052 lines through a real save), not the fixers — arms 1-3 do; a snapshot naming real issues would let a control modify the repository's own entries. The header now says so in those words

orchestrator_adjudication.finding: goal-mode.md §5.3 lists release as roadmap-authoritative while §4.1 calls it a projection; the code implements §4.1
orchestrator_adjudication.action: §5.3 amended in this PR: release is held on the roadmap but decided by the milestone (§4.1, RR-RELEASE); pmat work sync projects it and is its only writer. Flagged for the operator in the PR body

orchestrator_adjudication.finding: The grace window is applied per pair, not per field; a recent update to one field hides stale drift on the other
orchestrator_adjudication.action: §5.2 defines the clock per pair — now − max(item.updated, issue.updated_at) — and neither surface carries per-field timestamps; per-field tolerance would invent a clock the data does not have

orchestrator_adjudication.finding: Widening the open-item universe to every non-terminal status (blocked, review) defies the spec's {planned, inprogress} and breaks CB-2114 consistency
orchestrator_adjudication.action: deliberate and documented in the module doc: a blocked item with no issue is as invisible to GitHub as a planned one; is_open() is pub so CB-2114/CB-2115 inherit one definition by construction; test blocked_and_review_items_are_open. Lane 3's citation (mod.rs:1329) is past EOF
the test now computes the sorted write-sets of both directions and asserts Full equals their union (three writes) and skips nothing

orchestrator_adjudication.finding: check_only_passes_on_a_bijection sets json=true but asserts nothing about stdout
orchestrator_adjudication.action: report_json is asserted directly: report_json_carries_the_verdict_and_the_classes parses the document and checks coherent, grace_minutes, counts and the first finding's class and reason; control arm 2 asserts the same shape end to end

orchestrator_adjudication.finding: No test asserts the Skip reason for a release drift in the yaml-to-github direction
Commit 6d6d75168's message says three notes: fields; the diff re-flows one notes: field (PMAT-707, 30 lines to 1) and re-quotes PMAT-720's three acceptance_criteria strings
orchestrator_adjudication.action: recorded here and in the receipt rather than rewriting history the quorum already judged; values proven equal by parsing both sides (python yaml.safe_load, 278 items, equal)

orchestrator_adjudication.finding: Arm 4 will fail on a legitimate future hand-wrapped edit
orchestrator_adjudication.action: that is the invariant: a hand-wrapped entry re-flows on the next save and buries real diffs (§4.2); the failure message names the measured canonicaliser (pmat work edit <id> --priority <its current priority>)

orchestrator_adjudication.action: orchestrator's counting error in the prompt; no effect on the review (the range was named explicitly)

orchestrator_adjudication.finding: Three of lane 3's citations are past EOF (mod.rs:1329, mod.rs:1648, tests.rs:2517)
orchestrator_adjudication.action: those three claims were re-grounded by the orchestrator before adjudication (grace per pair: refuted on the spec's formula; universe widening: refuted; release-skip test: confirmed and added)
